title: Tighten artifact registration guidance
body:
Updates the `add_artifact_or_reference` tool description, `isArtifact` input description, and first-turn `ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION` so the model has a clear eligibility test for what to register.

**Problem:** the current text says artifacts are "notable results you produced beyond ordinary workspace edits, such as a report written outside the workspace." That makes location the signal, so anything persisted outside the workspace (scratch JSON, run-tracking records, cached data) reads as registrable.

**Change:**
- Register only deliverables the user requested, or standalone results they are clearly likely to reopen, download, or reuse.
- Default to no registration; it's not an inventory of everything saved.
- Explicitly exclude scratch files, caches, logs, intermediate results, and configuration snapshots unless requested.
- State that persistence or location outside the workspace is not an eligibility signal.
- Never create, copy, or relocate a file solely to have something to register.

Prose-only change; all phrases pinned by existing tests are preserved. `artifactServerTools.test.ts` and `chatContributions.test.ts` pass.

title: Add a crisp font-rendering option for macOS terminals
body:
- Add `terminal.integrated.fontRendering` on macOS with `inherit` (default) and `crisp`.
- Opt into pixel-level antialiasing for high-DPI terminal text without changing the editor, sidebar, theme colors, font family, size, or weight. Other displays continue to inherit the workbench font policy.
- Apply the terminal style before WebGL initialization and clear cached glyphs after the style changes, so existing text updates without clearing the buffer or reloading the window.
- Reuse the same helper for normal, detached, and sticky-scroll terminals. Detached updates continue through the existing centralized configuration listener.
- Add coverage for the unchanged default, initial attachment, live mode changes, cache-refresh ordering, unchanged font/theme options, and detached terminals.

The rendering comparison pointed to font-smoothing policy as the significant appearance difference. This is an opt-in style preference, not a new renderer or an increase in resolution. The separate xterm alpha-blending experiment, texture-filtering changes, native-renderer ideas, and demo color overrides are intentionally outside this PR; no xterm dependency or source changes are required.

### Validation

- `GOMAXPROCS=2 npm run transpile-client`
- `GOMAXPROCS=2 npm run typecheck-client`
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/xterm/xtermTerminal.test` — 24 passing.
- Targeted ESLint for the changed TypeScript files and stylelint for `terminalFontRendering.css`.

### Manual review cases

1. On a macOS HiDPI display, compare `inherit` and `crisp` using the same font and theme in panel/editor terminals. Check that surrounding workbench text and terminal colors do not change.
2. Toggle the mode with text already visible. The glyph appearance should update without clearing terminal content; sticky-scroll and detached terminal output should follow the same policy.
3. Check a lower-DPI display or move the terminal between displays: `crisp` should not force pixel antialiasing below the existing HiDPI threshold.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The HiDPI policy comes from the existing [`workbench.fontAliasing` CSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01/src/vs/workbench/browser/media/style.css#L178-L193), applied to the terminal element rather than the entire workbench.
- The cache-refresh API comes from [`XtermTerminal.forceRedraw`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/xterm/xtermTerminal.ts#L640-L642). Cached glyphs need to be regenerated after changing their inherited rendering policy.
- Detached-terminal update ordering follows [`TerminalService._ensureDetachedTerminalListeners`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalService.ts#L1142-L1175), without introducing another listener for every detached instance.
- The CSS-to-rasterization behavior is informed by Chromium's [`CanvasRenderingContext2D::ResolveFont`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/bfe29217d60b6ee25ce4e4b2c0abcd6361ae6eb6/third_party/blink/renderer/modules/canvas/canvas2d/canvas_rendering_context_2d.cc#L571-L638), which resolves the font using the canvas element's computed style, and xterm's [`TextureAtlas._drawToCache`](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/08ad9a4de9252f387cc5fbf68aa3d98e0ba8a0b7/addons/addon-webgl/src/TextureAtlas.ts#L472-L482), which attaches the raster canvas to the terminal.

title: fix: re-assert active editor context on workspace trust change
body:
Fixes #335608

Bug repro
1. Open a folder in Restricted Mode (untrusted) with a file open in the active editor.
2. Open Workspace Trust editor and choose Trust.
3. Return to the editor without switching editors/tabs.
4. File > Save remains greyed/disabled even though trust is now granted.

Root cause
Workspace trust transitions do not fire active-editor events, so stale activeEditor context keys persist. File > Save precondition on that context never re-evaluates until the active editor changes.

Fix
Re-observe the active editor on workspaceTrustService.onDidChangeTrust in EditorGroupView, re-asserting context keys immediately after a trust transition.

Validation
- eslint clean on touched file
- tsc --noEmit: 0 errors
- gulp compile-client: ok (~15s)
- Manual dev-window before/after: pre-fix Save greyed after granting trust (screenshot); post-fix Save stays enabled

title: Fix Agent Host sandbox synchronization and refactor shared picker logic
body:
## Summary

fixes #335494

Follow-up to #335364. Fix sandbox configuration and permission-picker behavior across the editor and Agents window, and consolidate the shared Agent Host sandbox logic.

## Bugs fixed

- **Wrong platform's sandbox setting:** Resolve the operating system of the session's Agent Host rather than assuming the renderer's platform when selecting Windows versus non-Windows sandbox settings. Cache the lookup per connection and log resolution failures.
- **Stale permission pickers after host changes:** Observe the resolved sandbox setting, refresh trigger state, and close open permission/mode menus when the setting changes. Ignore late OS responses from a previously selected connection or a disposed delegate.
- **Sandbox updates delayed until another turn:** Apply effective SDK sandbox configuration when settings change while a session is idle, not only while a turn is active. Retain active-turn abort behavior when applying configuration fails.
- **SDK sandbox configuration skipped with custom terminal tools:** Apply the effective SDK configuration at launch and during subsequent updates regardless of the custom-terminal flag, including an explicit `{ enabled: false }` state when disabled. Preserve fail-closed handling of rejected SDK updates.
- **Malformed merge resolutions:** Remove duplicated imports, declarations, callbacks, conditionals, and tests while retaining incoming changes from `main`.

## Refactoring

- Extract `getAgentHostOperatingSystem` as the shared, connection-scoped OS resolver for editor and Agents-window consumers.
- Extract `applySandboxConfig` so session launch and live updates share SDK result validation and logging.
- Simplify sandbox-setting selection by removing the unused custom-terminal argument and outdated comments describing skipped SDK configuration.
- Expose a reusable dropdown `hide()` operation and an observable sandbox-setting ID so picker surfaces can respond consistently to asynchronous host resolution.
- Update related test fixtures and service stubs, and add coverage for host OS resolution, connection changes, idle updates, and SDK sandbox application.

## Validation

- Core build/typecheck: **0 errors**; editor Problems panel clear.
- Refreshed all compiled client output with `npm run transpile-client` after detecting stale pre-merge output.
- Targeted tests across the Copilot session/launcher and permission/mode/config pickers: **627 passed, 1 failed**.
- Remaining failure: the existing compact-picker layout assertion compares a measured gap of `5.999988555908203` with exactly `6` in `agentHostChatInputPicker.test.ts`. Left unchanged because it is unrelated to these merge repairs.
- Commit hygiene checks passed; signing and verification hooks were retained.

Draft for review of the follow-up fixes and refactoring. No new end-to-end UI validation was performed as part of the merge repair.

![Solarized Dark: full Code OSS workbench](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f22e6d6b-e1de-4e6d-b9f1-d8d3dc87d6fd)

### Solarized Light

![Solarized Light: full Code OSS workbench](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22321cac-efd6-4d50-ba88-d998d9e7ef89)

</details>

## Design

- **Tab and background:** the selected tab uses `editor.background`; the inactive strip and tabs share `editorGroupHeader.tabsBackground`, composited once over the document surface for translucent customizations. There are no gaps between tabs, so adjacent hover begins at the selected tab's edge. Inactive labels use `tab.inactiveForeground`, with explicit theme customizations preserved.
- **Edges and border:** the first tab is flush with the document's left boundary; the final tab retains its curved shoulder. High-contrast themes outline the selected tab and document as one well, using `focusBorder` for the active group and `contrastBorder` for inactive groups. The empty editor retains a boundary after the last tab closes. Normal themes reserve the same geometry with a transparent stroke.
- **Wrapped and pinned rows:** only the bottom row connects to the document. Upper wrapped rows and separate pinned rows use symmetric pills; selected tabs keep the document background on every row. Upper-row hover and its action mask share one composited surface, without shifting the close icon. Active sticky shoulders paint above neighboring sticky tabs. Row fills stay equal at 28px default / 24px compact.
- **Text truncation:** tabs retain natural Fit sizing. Under compression, the filename keeps its first complete grapheme, ellipsis, and extension, with space reserved for badges and actions. Dotfiles retain the leading dot plus the next grapheme. Extensions are protected only when the title matches the resource filename; arbitrary dotted titles remain fully ellipsizable. Preview italics and strikethrough cover the extension too. The full name remains available in the hover and ARIA label.
- **Icon-slot collapse:** file icons and their slots yield space before filename identity is lost, and return when the editor widens. Explicit compact pinned tabs retain their icon-only behavior.
- **Actions and scrolling:** selected close actions and dirty indicators remain visible; clean inactive close actions appear on hover or keyboard focus. Hidden close slots do not intercept pointer input. Automatic reveal reserves both shoulders and the selected action, while first tabs and row starts stay flush. Deliberate partial scrolling uses a cap and shoulder to finish the visible boundary.
- **Palette scope:** theme-level inactive colors also affect classic tabs. Quiet Light uses a `#E4E4E4` strip against the `#F5F5F5` document, `#54494B` inactive/modern-hover text, and `#765500` warning text. Its warning color applies theme-wide, not only to tabs.

## Accessibility and consistency

| Area | Validation / consideration |
| --- | --- |
| Text contrast | Adjusted default-theme ordinary inactive labels pass 4.5:1 at rest and hover. Quiet Light's minimum is **4.995:1 across 21 tested filename states**, including warning decorations, hover, inactive groups, and upper-row selection. |
| Contrast exceptions | Unchanged Solarized Dark has a 4.23:1 resting sample; Solarized Light has 3.57:1 resting / 3.84:1 hover samples. Custom themes and every decoration color are not covered by these results. |
| Keyboard and accessible names | Tests preserve the complete filename in ARIA labels and reveal inactive close actions on keyboard focus. Automatic reveal retains focus-ring clearance at the viewport edge. |
| High contrast | Dark/Light HC checks cover one connected well outline, active/inactive groups, solid multi-selection versus dashed keyboard focus, and no geometry shift. Single/hidden-tab modes retain their editor-card frame. |
| Responsive layout | Tests cover equal row heights, selected fill on every row, hover-stable corners, filename/badge/action space, icon collapse and recovery, fractional-width reveal, and selection after closing scrolled tabs. |
| Style boundaries | Tests cover connected-mode gating, Pill colors, and explicit foreground customizations. Agents-window pill tabs remain unchanged. |

These are targeted automated and visual checks, not an end-to-end screen-reader audit or comprehensive WCAG certification.

## Validation

- **99 targeted tab/theme/label tests** pass with fresh client transpilation, including Unicode and dotfile compression, suffix styling, left/right reveal, empty HC frames, translucent strip colors, hover action masks, and fixture theme isolation. Client type checking also passes.
- Geometry/theme coverage includes **90 fixtures / 270 rendered states** and **45 viewport-edge fixtures / 60 states**. All **24 Quiet Light connected fixtures** pass render/dispose checks.
- **CI:** [Current PR checks](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335605/checks) include screenshot baselines, fixture rendering, compilation, and Code OSS cross-platform tests.
- **51 focused render/dispose checks** pass, including connected selection across all 15 themes and sampled upper wrapped/pinned selection, hover, compact density, and narrow labels. Four additional sticky-viewport checks pass across default dark/light and both HC themes.
- **Media fidelity:** both default PNGs retain their native 2x pixels; all **1,205 decoded video frames** match the source RGB pixels exactly. Chromium playback and chapter seeking were verified.

## Enable

```jsonc
{
  "workbench.experimental.modernUI": true,
  "workbench.experimental.modernUIEditorTabStyle": "connected"
}
```

Use `workbench.editor.wrapTabs` for multiple rows and `workbench.editor.tabSizing: "shrink"` for constrained widths. Set the tab style to `"pill"` to compare. The tab-style setting requires Modern UI to be enabled.

# Automation provider configuration and custom-agent follow-ups

## Contents

- [Context](#context)
- [Stack and review scope](#stack-and-review-scope)
- [Restored fixes](#restored-fixes)
- [Intentional limits](#intentional-limits)
- [Commit inventory](#commit-inventory)
- [Validation](#validation)
- [Draft readiness and CI](#draft-readiness-and-ci)
- [Exact-tree guarantee](#exact-tree-guarantee)

## Context

An automation separates its execution target from its provider-owned session template. The target selects the provider, workspace, isolation mode, and branch. The template holds model configuration, custom-agent selection, and native preferences such as Mode, Approvals, and Cloud Sandbox.

Editing and executing an automation must preserve those preferences without turning them into permanent permission grants. The provider's current capabilities and policy still determine the effective runtime behavior. Both the browser fallback executor and the durable Agent Host executor must pass the selected model and custom agent to the first turn.

## Stack and review scope

This draft extracts the eight provider-configuration and custom-agent fixes from the already-merged [#335018](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335018).

The draft is [#335595](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335595). It intentionally remains a draft with automatic merging disabled.

The review stack is:

1. [#335591](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335591): the full revert of the original fifteen-fix PR.
2. [#335593](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335593) (`ulugbekna/fix-automation-worktree-gating`): the smaller seven-commit worktree-discovery, branch-picker, validation, and startup repair.
3. This draft, `ulugbekna/automation-config-followups`: the remaining eight logical commits, based on the smaller worktree branch rather than `main`.

Review this draft against [#335593](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335593), on `ulugbekna/fix-automation-worktree-gating`. Its diff is limited to ten files covering provider configuration, custom-agent execution, and their regression tests.

There are no standalone worktree-capability, New Worktree gating, branch-search, or worktree-pending-startup changes in this draft. Those belong to its base. There are also no shared ActionList or IME changes. The Codex worktree changes here specifically preserve custom-agent identity and instructions during worktree execution.

## Restored fixes

### Cloud model selection and canonical preferences

Restoring a Cloud model previously updated the visible selection without consistently updating the extension's model option. The shared model-update path now synchronizes both representations, including when the extension's option catalogue arrives later.

Canonical template configuration takes precedence over legacy mode and permission aliases. Unknown provider values remain intact so saving an automation does not erase preferences the current provider cannot interpret. Unsupported Cloud permission changes are no-ops: they do not silently replace the saved canonical preference or change Cloud's effective default permissions.

### Fallback CLI approvals

The fallback CLI keeps a restored approval preference separately from its policy-effective value. Current policy controls display and execution; an unchanged saved preference survives capture so editing an automation does not accidentally replace its intent with a temporary policy restriction.

### Cloud Sandbox execution

Cloud Sandbox is part of the automation's own captured template and is restored independently of the ordinary composer's remembered choice. Legacy definitions retain their previous fallback behavior until their first capture. The existing Sandbox control is available in Automation controls and remains gated by AI visibility.

The original regression `does not enable unsupported Cloud worktree or branch configuration` is rehomed into this commit rather than the smaller worktree PR. It asserts that Cloud does not acquire worktree support, isolation or branch values, and captures `{ autoApprove: Default, useSandbox: false }`. It requires these Cloud fixes and therefore belongs with them.

### First-turn custom agents

The Agent Host executor inherits the creation-time custom agent into the first message, independently of model inheritance. An explicit first-message selection still takes precedence. Fallback-provider tests also cover sending the restored custom agent on the first automation request.

### Codex custom agents in worktrees and restored sessions

Codex resolves a selected native workspace agent against the host-owned worktree when preparing customization launch. Host worktree metadata and canonical repository roots establish the relationship; the persisted agent URI is not rewritten.

This keeps agent instructions available on repeated turns, after reapplying the same selection, and after provider reload, including linked source checkouts. Plugin and external selections are not redirected. Existing telemetry injection and workspace-less customization directories are preserved.

### Native configuration controls

Automation controls reuse the provider's existing enum and boolean pickers so equivalent settings remain consistent across surfaces. Generic controls do not duplicate the dedicated worktree, branch, Mode, or Approvals controls and do not expose transient session-only configuration.

The existing Dev Container handoff remains separate. The extraction preserves the current picker constructor options and the upstream relocation of the Dev Container control.

## Intentional limits

- Cloud worktrees, workspace-less Cloud sessions, and Cloud custom agents remain unsupported.
- Saved mode and approval values are preferences, not grants that bypass current policy.
- Existing remote/container hosts continue to use their provider boundary; transient local Dev Container handoff is not a new template field.
- No new protocol fields, dependencies, settings, policy channels, or architecture changes are introduced.
- This is a scope split of existing fixes, not a new feature or refactor.

## Commit inventory

| Original commit | Extracted commit | Logical fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1b7e62e17e3` | `df4ac6382b1` | Synchronize restored Cloud model options |
| `1f44f2eaac3` | `173f1775aba` | Preserve canonical Cloud configuration |
| `507adda226c` | `deabc94ebcb` | Ignore unsupported Cloud permission overrides |
| `4d4c118577e` | `f870ec0dc06` | Clamp restored CLI approval preferences |
| `afc2e297266` | `558f45ca91d` | Persist Cloud Sandbox choices and rehome the Cloud-only regression |
| `6eb7c964c2a` | `a2edf971fb6` | Retain custom agents on the first run turn |
| `d5884de7f7e` | `564cd05e5e5` | Retain Codex workspace agents across worktree turns and reloads |
| `c461304d323` | `66ee5f960b0` | Expose native provider configuration controls |

There are exactly eight commits above base `790568f194ff986449c9c1fb62142149fc8e09d7`. The draft head is `66ee5f960b032875783ab5c1779499cb4142cab2`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run transpile-client`: passed.
- The five requested test files ran in one existing Electron runner invocation: **308 passing, 0 failing**.
- `git diff --check` against the stacked base: passed.


The passing coverage includes the rehomed Cloud worktree/branch regression, canonical and late Cloud model restoration, Sandbox feature gating, policy-effective CLI approvals, native configuration controls, first-message selections, and Codex worktree/provider-reload behavior.

## Draft readiness and CI

The branch is pushed and clean, with eight commits across ten files. The current GitHub check snapshot reports CLA and Dependencies Check passing, VS Code PR Check pending, and no failed checks or unresolved review comments.

The main Code OSS, Component Fixtures and CodeQL workflows only trigger for pull requests targeting `main` or release branches. They are not running for this draft's feature-branch base. Local validation is complete, but this must not be described as full GitHub CI coverage.

title: Fix forked process console forwarding reporting shared references as circular
body:
While fixing `safeStringify` in #335589 I noticed that `src/bootstrap-fork.ts` has its own copy of the same replacer. `safeToString`, which forwards `console.*` calls from forked processes to the parent when `VSCODE_VERBOSE_LOGGING` is set (the pty host, the file watcher and the agent host starters all set it), pushes every object into a `seen` array and never removes anything. So an object that is logged twice, or referenced from two properties, reaches the parent as `"[Circular]"` after its first occurrence, even though there is no cycle.

With a forked fixture that runs

```ts
const shared = { value: 1 };
console.log(shared, { a: shared, b: shared }, circular); // circular.self = circular
```

the `__$console` message the parent receives is:

```
before: [{"value":1},{"a":"[Circular]","b":"[Circular]"},{"name":"circular","self":"[Circular]"}]
after:  [{"value":1},{"a":{"value":1},"b":{"value":1}},{"name":"circular","self":"[Circular]"}]
```

The fix is the same one as in #335589 and in `stableStringify` (#327398). The replacer only tracks the current ancestor path, and uses `this` (the holder) to pop subtrees that are finished. Real cycles are still replaced with `"[Circular]"`. I removed the `isObject` helper because every object has to go on the stack for the holder check to work. Together with the `Array.isArray` check, the only objects it left out were RegExp and Date instances, and a Date has already been turned into a string by `toJSON` by the time the replacer sees it.

How I tested it: I added a case to `processes.integrationTest.ts` that forks `bootstrap-fork` with a new `fork_console` fixture and checks the forwarded arguments, including a genuine cycle. It fails against the current `bootstrap-fork.ts` with the "before" output above and passes with the fix, and the other tests in the file still pass. I ran it with `test/unit/node/index.js --run src/vs/base/test/node/processes/processes.integrationTest.ts`, with the Node version check commented out because the machine I used has Node 22. eslint is clean on the changed files and `typecheck-client` reports nothing in them.

There is no issue for this that I could find. This PR doesn't depend on #335589, they touch different files.

# Fix falsely disabled automation worktree selection

## Contents

- [Stack and purpose](#stack-and-purpose)
- [Root cause](#root-cause)
- [Included fixes](#included-fixes)
- [Explicit exclusions](#explicit-exclusions)
- [Validation](#validation)

## Stack and purpose

This is the smaller replacement for the worktree portion of [#335018](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335018).

It is based on the revert branch in [#335591](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335591), not directly on main, so this PR's diff contains only the seven worktree/startup fixes. Review and land the revert first, then this PR. The remaining provider configuration changes are held in [draft #335595](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335595), stacked on this branch.

The goal is that **New Worktree is selectable for a supported Codex, Claude, or other Agent Host automation target**, while unavailable or non-repository targets are rejected instead of silently promising isolation.

## Root cause

The automation dialog read a session-type capability that was hard-coded to Copilot CLI. Codex and Claude therefore appeared unsupported even though the Agent Host owns worktree isolation for their sessions.

The dialog also used the local Git extension to discover every target's repository and branches. That cannot discover repositories on a remote Agent Host. Merely removing the Copilot-only flag would leave remote targets incorrectly unavailable.

## Included fixes

1. Advertise host-owned worktree configuration for all advertised Agent Host agents. Workspace-specific support still comes from the host's schema.
2. Obtain workspace support, current branch, and branch choices through a provider-owned operation. Remote search reuses the resolved context, and partial completion results do not falsely mark saved branches unavailable.
3. Allow opting out of a saved Worktree selection when support disappears.
4. After opting out, require normal repository availability before Worktree can be selected again; a retained branch is not a bypass.
5. Validate workspace-specific worktree support when the configure tool creates or changes an explicit worktree target. Unsupported/missing options reject the target, cancellation makes no changes, and provider errors are not silently treated as success. Legacy providers without the optional operation retain their previous behavior.
6. Coalesce duplicate repository lookups from related target/provider notifications.
7. Mark generated session IDs worktree-pending before eager provider startup. This prevents Codex prewarming in the source checkout before host isolation is ready; failed creation cleans the pending state.

The implementation remains provider-neutral in shared Sessions code. Tests cover supported provider choices, remote branch discovery/search, unavailable targets, cancellation and recovery, and startup ordering.

## Explicit exclusions

This PR does **not** change:

- Cloud model restoration, compatibility fields, or Sandbox routing;
- fallback CLI approval-policy preference handling;
- custom-agent first-turn inheritance or Codex custom-agent restoration;
- provider-native configuration toolbars;
- the shared ActionList implementation or its tests.

Those provider-configuration and custom-agent fixes are held for separate draft review. The shared IME fix is independently tracked in [#335578](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335578).

Until that IME fix lands, cancelling composition during a pending remote branch search without changing the query can leave the picker loading. Changing the query or reopening it remains the workaround. This smaller PR does not claim to fix that shared-component edge case.

## Validation

- **977 targeted unit tests passed**, with 27 existing pending tests.
- **Five strict real-provider replay scenarios passed**, covering host branch configuration, Copilot/Claude/Codex working directories, and automation configuration after host restart.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Changed-file ESLint, `git diff --check`, and normal commit hygiene passed.

title: agentHost: release edit timing correlations when turns end
body:
## What and why

Stop long-lived Copilot sessions from retaining the SDK turn and interaction IDs of every completed host turn. This follows up on the [performance review comment on #331983](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331983#discussion_r3976023683).

Previously, these string-to-string correlations remained in session-level maps after their host turn ended. They now belong to the active `CopilotTurn` and are cleared on disposal, covering completion, cancellation, failure, discard, replacement, and session teardown without scanning historical entries.

## Routing behavior

A delayed model-call event for a completed turn is now dropped by the provider rather than forwarded with the old turn ID for downstream rejection. An unknown interaction ID never falls back to a reused SDK turn ID. Steering transfers the active SDK-turn association to the promoted turn, and SDK `assistant.turn_end` alone does not expire correlations while the host turn is still active.

Regression coverage checks retained-key counts over repeated turns, terminal paths, steering telemetry, and late-event routing. This addresses unnecessary ID retention; it does not claim a measured user-visible performance improvement.
## Steering in timing data

Turn-completion telemetry now distinguishes turns that started from a provider-promoted steering message (`startedWithSteering`) from turns that received a steering submission while active (`receivedSteering`). This lets analyses separate fresh-prompt timing from steering continuations, including turns that fall into both categories.

TTFE continues to be recorded for both populations, preserving edits measured before steering. A steering turn's TTFE is its own model-dispatch prefix, not the combined work across the preceding turn. `receivedSteering` records submission, even if the message is later removed or never consumed; ordinary queued follow-ups do not set either flag. Historical rows without these fields have unknown steering classification, rather than meaning false.

title: sessions: add rich GitHub reference previews
body:
## Summary

Exploratory follow-up to #335448, building on the first-level title work from #335387.

This proposal adds a compact issue/PR preview to Agents Window reference pills so users can identify a GitHub object and decide whether to open it without leaving their current context.

## Design rationale

- **Progressive disclosure:** collections keep the existing scannable list; focusing a row reveals detail. A single reference shows the same detail directly.
- **Source-product hierarchy:** GitHub's own hover cards inform the order of information, while VS Code continues to own typography, color, spacing, popup chrome, focus, and keyboard behavior. Collection rows lead with the lifecycle icon, followed by the canonical title and a muted trailing ID.
- **Bounded transient content:** the card provides identity and enough context to make a decision, rather than becoming a full issue reader.
- **Consistent information budget:** standalone and collection cards contain the same information; only their outer density differs.

The resulting card order is repository/date → title/ID → lifecycle and CI state → bounded description → PR branches → author. Open and draft pull requests show the shared overall checks state as `Checks pending`, `Checks failed`, or `Checks passed`; closed, merged, and no-check states stay quiet. Pending uses GitHub's familiar attention-colored static dot rather than a spinner or sync metaphor because the aggregate may include both queued and running checks. Both status pills use neutral text and surfaces, while their icons carry restrained semantic color.

Descriptions are normalized from Markdown and bounded to 200 Unicode code points. Visible titles are bounded to 80 Unicode code points. The final visible title word and linked ID are grouped so the number cannot interrupt the sentence or become clipped at narrow widths.

#335448 also explores a full Markdown reader across broader GitHub-reference surfaces; this iteration focuses on the compact pill-hover treatment.

## What inspired the design

- **GitHub hover cards:** provenance first, title and ID as the lead, state next, then context, routing details, and authorship/viewer context.
- **GitLab and GitHub PR experiences:** emphasize identity, state, and short context before secondary metadata.
- **Linear/Slack unfurls:** keep transient previews concise and action-oriented instead of reproducing the full work item.
- **JetBrains and VS Code GitHub PR lists:** use an overall checks result in compact references, while reserving individual checks, review state, and denser metadata for persistent triage surfaces.
- **Existing VS Code patterns:** reuse the issue/PR hover components, ActionList list/dialog semantics, SessionSummaryHover hierarchy, branch pills, popup chrome, focus indicators, and spacing tokens.

Those examples drove the current boundary: enough content to understand and route the reference, with individual checks, labels, reactions, comments, assignees, and full Markdown left to richer or persistent surfaces.

## Collection item interactions

### Pull request collection

![Pull request collection expanded with the first-level list and second-level rich preview showing draft and checks-pending status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99177b86-d08d-41be-b3b6-9cedb3438409)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d1e6b01-ffb4-47f7-9283-8c590a56ba10

Starts on the focused Pull Requests parent pill, opens the first-level list, moves across PR states and the live overall CI result, then traverses Copy URL, repository, ID, and base/head branches. The clip follows the complete reverse Shift+Tab sequence back through every card control and row action.

### Issue collection

![Issue collection expanded with the first-level list and second-level rich issue preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c2a33a4-52db-41e7-ae15-99bab03661da)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9434801-d04b-4a3b-beff-011ad176ac18

Starts on the focused Issues parent pill, opens the first-level list, covers long-title/closed/open rows, then traverses Copy URL, repository, and ID before reversing through each control back to the list.

## Single-reference interactions

A single reference skips the list but keeps the same information budget.

### Single pull request

![Single pull request chip expanded with its rich preview showing draft and checks-pending status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4842658c-f51d-470d-ba5d-cda15e140368)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf5da59b-2bfd-4add-9a31-a92c4586a9f9

Uses Shift+Tab and ArrowRight to focus the direct PR chip, then opens its hover with the live overall CI result and moves through repository, linked ID, and base/head branch controls.

### Single issue

![Single issue chip expanded with its rich issue preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48e07143-9e6b-4479-8e69-6b27b41a81ec)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26ef0069-4969-4151-8ae2-cbc6cd7f1b32

Uses Shift+Tab and ArrowRight to focus the direct issue chip, then opens its hover and moves through repository and linked ID.

## Keyboard and screen-reader behavior

- **Collections:** Shift+Tab from the chat input focuses the first pill; Left/Right moves between pills.
- **Collections:** Enter/Space opens the list, Up/Down moves through rows, and the metadata card follows the focused item.
- **Collections:** Tab moves through Copy URL, repository, resource ID, and PR branch controls; Shift+Tab returns to Copy URL.
- **Single references:** Enter/Space activates the reference directly; pointer hover exposes the same detail content and its links/branch controls.
- The listbox retains keyboard focus while the named detail dialog remains available in screen-reader reading order.
- Rows announce the full resource title, lifecycle state, and overall CI result. The detail card reads provenance → title/ID → lifecycle/CI state → description → branches → author.
- Focusing a bounded title's ID reveals the full canonical title; blur restores the compact title.

## Implementation

- reuses `ChatDropdownPillActionViewItem`, `ActionListWidget`, `createIssueHoverElement`, and `createPullRequestHoverElement`
- keeps standalone and collection content identical
- reads the existing shared CI model; no additional GitHub request path is introduced
- polls CI for open pull requests, including drafts, while keeping review-thread icon refinement limited to non-drafts
- preserves GitHub's distinct `Duplicate` and `Not planned` issue terminology
- makes ActionList and managed-hover padding ownership explicit instead of using compensating offsets
- uses standard ActionWidget border, radius, background, shadow, and spacing tokens
- uses measured panel dimensions for viewport positioning

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint and stylelint
- focused ActionList and Sessions toolbar tests: 103 passing
- dark/light and keyboard-focus fixtures
- standalone issue and PR paths
- live Open, Draft, Closed, Merged, Completed, and Not planned resources
- live draft PR with pending checks; unit coverage for pending, passing, failing, and no-check states
- 567-character title and 300px-width stress cases
- linked ID remains fully visible and focusing it does not scroll clipped content

## Related

- #335448
- #335383
- #335387

title: actionWidget: fix: resume interrupted IME searches
body:
## Summary

Resume an asynchronous ActionList search that IME composition interrupted, even when composition ends with the original query. Do not repeat searches that already completed or failed, and do not let a stale request's cleanup disturb a newer request.

This is a focused follow-up to [#328269](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328269). The shared-component fixes are separated from [#335018](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335018) so the automation changes can be reviewed and landed independently.

Only two files change:

- [actionList.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/66fb14d02a916676638641c6e0c21749253487a6/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts): the existing filter-input guard and asynchronous request cleanup.
- [actionList.test.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/66fb14d02a916676638641c6e0c21749253487a6/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts): four regression cases using the existing widget helpers and deferred promises.

## Background and failure

ActionList can filter an existing list locally or delegate filtering to an asynchronous provider through `onFilter`. For asynchronous filtering, it owns the current request's cancellation token source in a `MutableDisposable`.

The existing IME handling deliberately defers filtering during composition. Intermediate input can contain uncommitted text, and rebuilding or laying out the result list can disrupt the IME candidate window. Starting a composition also cancels an outstanding search so its results cannot update the list during composition.

Both `compositionend` and the accompanying `input` event eventually use the same value-change handler. That handler originally skipped every unchanged query to deduplicate those events.

The failure occurs when:

1. The user searches for `release`, starting an asynchronous request.
2. IME composition starts before the request finishes, cancelling that request.
3. Composition ends with `release` again, either after intermediate text or without a committed change.
4. The unchanged-query guard suppresses a replacement request, while the original request's results are correctly ignored because it was cancelled.

The pending query therefore never supplies fresh results until the user changes the search text again.

## How the fix works

### 1. An unchanged query can restart an interrupted request

The input handler still ignores all changes while composition is active. Outside composition, it skips an unchanged query only when there is no cancelled current request.

This lets `compositionend` restart the search that composition interrupted. The restart immediately replaces the cancelled token source with a live one, so the trailing `input` event for the same text does not issue another request. Existing checks continue to reject results from the cancelled request.

### 2. Settled requests stop looking like pending work

Relaxing the guard alone would introduce an unnecessary retry: previously the current token source remained stored after a search completed or failed. A later `compositionstart` could cancel that already-settled source and make the unchanged query look interrupted.

The asynchronous chain now has a `finally` handler that clears the token source only when:

- it is still the widget's current request; and
- it has not been cancelled.

The same cleanup runs after success or failure. Clearing through the existing `MutableDisposable` disposes the source without cancelling an already-settled token, so later composition cannot mark that search as interrupted.

The identity check is essential: an older request can settle after a newer request has replaced it. Its cleanup must not clear the newer request's cancellation state. Otherwise composition could neither reliably cancel nor restart the newer request.

A cancelled current request intentionally remains available as the retry signal, even if its promise has already settled. The existing replacement, hide, and disposal paths own its cleanup; no additional collection or long-lived listener is introduced.

## Scope and preserved behavior

- Local/static filtering remains unchanged.
- Composing text still does not drive filtering or intermediate list updates.
- Searches whose committed query changes still follow the existing request path.
- Completed and failed searches are not retried solely because composition leaves the query unchanged.
- Superseded results remain ignored, and superseded completions cannot clear newer request state.
- The existing error-handling behavior is preserved; this does not introduce a retry policy for failed searches.
- No public API, settings, commands, keybindings, labels, ARIA roles, styling, or layout rules change.
- No automation, Agents Window, or chat-picker production code is included.

The interaction remains focused and consistent: the IME retains ownership during composition, and only the interrupted committed query resumes afterward. This is not a visual redesign or a new interactive surface.

## Validation

Standalone validation against the main-based branch:

- `npm run transpile-client` succeeded and generated fresh output containing both fixes.
- **192 tests passed** across the five modules below.
- Both commits passed the normal pre-commit hygiene hook.
- `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/tabbedActionListWidget.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionWidgetDropdown.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostSessionConfigPicker.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatInputPicker.test.ts \
  --reporter dot
```

The new regression cases cover:

1. An interrupted search is restarted once when composition leaves the query unchanged; stale results stay hidden and the replacement results appear.
2. A successfully completed search is not retried or marked cancelled by a later unchanged composition.
3. A failed search is not retried or marked cancelled by a later unchanged composition.
4. Settling an older, superseded request does not lose the pending request's ability to be cancelled and retried by composition.

The tests explicitly send the trailing `input` event to verify deduplication. The existing suites also cover composition suppression, stale-result handling, keyboard and combobox behavior, disposable cleanup, and the two dynamic consumers.

Validation used synthetic browser composition events in the Electron unit runner. A native operating-system IME session and manual screen-reader pass were not rerun for this extraction.

title: fix: raise telemetry-extractor heap limit to prevent build OOM (build fix for vscode-engineering#3836)
body:
## Build failure

The `Generate lists of telemetry events` build task crashed with a V8 out-of-memory error while running `@vscode/telemetry-extractor`:

```
FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

The crash occurred near ~2052 MB. The remaining failed tasks in the build (1ES verify + crash/log publish) were downstream cascades of the extractor never producing its output paths.

## Root cause

`build/azure-pipelines/common/extract-telemetry.ts` invokes the extractor with plain `node "${extractor}" ...` and no heap flag, so it runs at V8's default ~2 GB old-space limit. The extractor loads telemetry declarations for the whole `sourceDir` tree into memory; as the tree grows it deterministically crosses that ceiling. This is a resource ceiling rather than a specific regression — no commit in the build window touches telemetry extraction.

## How the fix works

Both `node` extractor invocations now pass `--max-old-space-size=8192`, raising the old-space heap to 8 GB and giving extraction headroom well above the previous ~2 GB crash point. The flag is defined once as `extractorNodeOptions` and applied to both calls, with a comment documenting why. No behavior changes beyond the heap limit; telemetry output and error reporting are unchanged.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**. Culprit commit/PR: `not confirmed` — the failure is a deterministic build-tool heap ceiling, and the product commits in the build window do not touch telemetry extraction, so there is no code regression to revert. A bounded heap bump lands quickly and safely; a rollback would not address the OOM. Owners to consult: `@joaomoreno`

## Validation

Source inspection only. The change is confined to two shell command strings in a build script; the extractor binary and arguments are otherwise unchanged. CI validation happens when the telemetry extraction task runs in the pipeline. Local build/pipeline validation of this task was not run with the available tools.

## Risk

Low. The only effect is a higher permitted heap for a short-lived build subprocess. No product code or runtime behavior is affected.

title: Give IconLabel ownership of icon-label spacing
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Abandoned experiment.** The `IconLabel` audit was useful, but this implementation introduced a public option, runtime host tracking, consumer overrides, and extensive tests for a very small product effect. It is not part of the active proposal or stack. The retained conclusion is that `Button` already reuses `renderLabelWithIcons`, while the full `IconLabel` widget is a separate resource/list-label abstraction that does not need to change for #335350.

## Predictable UI composition - 4 of 4: `IconLabel` shared-control pilot

This is the fourth PR in the draft stack:

1. **#335345 - candidate token foundation:** register the proposed spacing and icon-size vocabulary.
2. **#335346 - candidate authoring guidance:** derive a property-agnostic ownership rule.
3. **#335350 - `WorkbenchButtonBar` pilot:** consolidate the button’s leading icon/spinner slot relationship.
4. **This PR - `IconLabel` pilot:** consolidate the shared resource/list-label icon relationship and migrate one production override.

This remains an experiment supporting #335354. It validates `IconLabel` as a second shared-control counterexample; it does not make every icon-label composition use this widget.

## Problem

`IconLabel` already owns the relationship between its leading icon and label, but its two rendering paths encoded the same geometry independently:

- file/product icon classes render through `::before` with a 16px width and 6px right padding;
- explicit `iconPath` values render a child node with a 16px width and 6px right margin.

Modern UI compact pinned tabs then removed both contributions with separate consumer selectors. The effective icon-only composition therefore depended on the consumer knowing both internal render paths.

## Pilot implementation

- Adds `IIconLabelValueOptions.iconLabelSpacing` with behavior-safe `default` and `none` variants. Omission preserves the existing 6px relationship.
- Gives both icon paths the shared `--vscode-iconSize-small` role. Relationship spacing uses `margin-inline-end`, keeping it outside the painted pseudo-element for RTL; predefined ThemeIcon optical padding stays inside a fixed 16px border-box. Every registered size variable retains its existing literal as a fallback for standalone Monaco.
- Keeps the explicit icon-path slot fixed while label text truncates.
- Threads the option through `ResourceLabel`.
- Makes `MultiEditorTabsControl` select `none` for compact pinned icon-only tabs from the actual `.modern-ui-tabs` composition signal (or the Sessions constructor flag), refreshes labels when that runtime signal changes during layout, and removes the two path-specific consumer overrides.
- Leaves ordinary labels, classic tabs, inline `$(icon)` segments, descriptions, hover behavior, and accessible names unchanged.

The full `IconLabel` widget is still not used inside `Button`; both controls already share the lower-level `renderLabelWithIcons` helper, while their leading-slot semantics remain distinct.

## Review findings addressed

- **Standalone Monaco:** every new size-variable use now carries the existing literal as its fallback, and a browser test masks the variables to verify both icon paths retain 16px/6px default geometry.
- **Blocking visual coverage:** both the shared `IconLabel` fixture and the Modern UI compact-pinned-tab fixture now set `blocksCi: true`; the rendered manifest confirms their `blocks-ci` label.
- **Modern UI host signal:** compact-tab spacing now follows the runtime `.modern-ui-tabs` ancestor used by regular workbench sizing as well as the Sessions constructor flag. Layout detects signal changes and redraws label variants; a unit test covers default → none → default transitions, and the production fixture throws unless it reaches the `none` branch.

title: automations: feat: add shareable automation blueprints
body:
## Summary

Add portable Automation blueprints that can be shared as `.automation.md` files or contributed as templates by Agent Plugins.

A blueprint is intentionally not a live Automation. It contains display metadata, a prompt, and a manual or local-time cron schedule, but excludes workspace/provider selection, models, permissions, enabled state, timestamps, and run history. Every import path opens the existing New Automation dialog for review and starts disabled.

Refs #335507

## User experience

### Share Automations as files

- Export a saved Automation from its card context menu.
- Import a `.automation.md` file from the Automations header.
- Drag one `.automation.md` file anywhere over the Automations view.
- Review the imported name, prompt, schedule, target, model, and isolation before creating it.
- Invalid files, unsupported cron expressions, fixed timezones, and multi-file drops fail with actionable errors.

Export normalizes the selected filename to exactly one `.automation.md` suffix.

### Discover templates from plugins

Agent Plugins may contribute Automation blueprints from:

- the default `automations/` directory
- additional `extensions.com.github.copilot.automations` paths

Enabled plugins expose valid blueprints as inert templates. Discovery never creates or schedules an Automation.

The Automations view presents two disclosures:

- **Built-in Templates** is always available. It starts expanded when there are no saved Automations and folded when saved Automations exist.
- **Templates from Plugins** appears when non-empty and follows the same default.

Expanded content aligns beneath the section title while the chevron remains in a disclosure gutter. Plugin cards display a **Plugin** badge and source attribution.

When Templates from Plugins is folded, newly added template IDs show a blue unread-style marker. Expanding the section records the currently visible IDs as seen. The profile-scoped machine-local snapshot prevents already-seen filesystem templates from being announced again after reopening the view.

## Portable format

Recurring Automation:

```markdown
---
version: 1
id: weekly-review
name: Weekly review
schedule:
  kind: cron
  expression: "0 9 * * 1"
  timeZone: local
---
Review this workspace for regressions.
```

Manual Automation:

```markdown
---
version: 1
id: review-on-demand
name: Review on demand
schedule:
  kind: manual
---
Review the current workspace.
```

The file format uses cron as the portable recurring representation while the current editor retains its Manual, Hourly, Daily, and Weekly presets. Import accepts only cron forms that can round-trip through that editor and rejects richer expressions rather than silently changing their meaning.

## Safety and authority boundaries

- Installing, discovering, or enabling a plugin never creates scheduled work.
- Imported and plugin-provided Automations start disabled.
- Blueprints cannot carry provider/workspace selection or durable permission grants.
- File import and drag-and-drop always use the same review dialog.
- `IAutomationService` remains the only mutation path, preserving provider routing and Agent Host authority.
- Disabled and policy-blocked plugins do not contribute templates.

## Accessibility

- Both template sections are keyboard-operable native disclosures.
- Focus moves safely when a populated view collapses a section containing focus.
- The blue visual marker is hidden from assistive technology; the summary reports the count of new templates.
- Accessibility Help explains sharing, disclosures, and new-template behavior.
- Accessible View lists both template groups and source attribution without reading full prompts.

## Validation

- 133 targeted blueprint, plugin-discovery, import/drop, and Automation view tests
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint
- targeted Stylelint
- layer validation
- `git diff --check`
- live Agents-window Code OSS verification of:

title: agentHost: preserve Codex threads across subscription switches and support session handoff between chatgpt app and vs code
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #335268. Restoring a native Codex conversation is not sufficient if selecting a Copilot model replaces its thread or saves provider-specific state that prevents a native client from continuing it.

- Reload the original thread when switching model providers instead of creating a replacement. Preserve turn-ID mappings, apply the requested provider before sending, and handle selection changes during an in-flight handoff.
- Before a native-to-Copilot handoff, ensure the effective user configuration contains a portable `vscode-proxy` alias using native OpenAI authentication. VS Code continues to override that alias with its process-local Copilot proxy. No endpoints, credentials, or global model/provider defaults are persisted.
- Opt threads with native history into portable reasoning handling. Strip account-bound encrypted reasoning from proxy requests and SSE/JSON responses before SDK persistence, retaining visible summaries, messages, tool calls/results, and usage. Ordinary Copilot-only traffic is unchanged.
- Honor the effective `CODEX_HOME` in the advanced-configuration action and preserve portability across cold restoration, forks, and subagents.

## Usage telemetry

- Add `agentHost.codexProviderSwitch` after `turn/start` accepts a turn on the same backing thread. Report bounded `fromProvider` / `toProvider` (`openai` or `copilot`) and `isDesktopThread` (original desktop provenance, not the most recent client).
- For a signed-in ChatGPT account, optionally include `chatgptWeeklyUsedPercentBucket`, rounded down to 0, 10, …, 100. Sample the existing cache before the turn; accept only an explicit seven-day window observed within five minutes and not past a known reset. Omit missing, invalid, nonweekly, expired, or stale samples and samples from a different account. Missing data is not zero. No quota requests, polling, or waits are added.
- Count successful retries once. Picker-only changes, metadata reads, setup-only resumes, failed sends, repeated same-provider turns, switches reverted before sending, and stale handoffs for replacement threads do not count. A fresh/prewarmed thread's initial provider selection is not a switch.
- Use the existing usage-telemetry service and consent settings. Do not report prompts, model names, paths, conversation IDs, arbitrary provider strings, email, plan, reset time, or exact quota percentages. Account-linked quota usage remains subject to normal telemetry/privacy review.
- This measures subscription handoffs observed by Agent Host, not app switches or activity performed entirely in other clients. The quota bucket enables aggregate correlation with quota pressure, not proof of why a user switched.

## Safety and limitations

- The first handoff may add the alias to the user configuration. Writes use the app-server configuration API, are serialized and version-checked, retry bounded version conflicts, and never overwrite an existing definition. Incompatible persistent settings fail before unsubscribing or changing the native thread.
- Metadata/history reads remain read-only. Native single-writer ownership is unchanged.
- This does not merge previously created duplicate threads, rewrite existing rollouts, or repair incompatible encrypted reasoning already persisted by older clients.

## Validation

- Client transpilation and TypeScript checking; targeted ESLint; staged hygiene; `git diff --check`.
- Telemetry follow-up: **514 passing** in the full Codex suite and **13 passing** in the existing telemetry-service/opt-out suite. Coverage includes both directions, desktop provenance, cold restoration, failure/retry, duplicate suppression, reverted selections, prewarm, changed backing identities, weekly-usage bucketing, freshness/reset boundaries, pre-turn sampling, and account-change isolation.
- Targeted Codex, configuration/environment/account, and orchestration suites: **1,003 passing, 16 pending**.
- Live Code OSS smoke test: five alternating native-auth/Copilot turns in one persisted thread, including an agent-host restart and a read-only tool call, using the bundled Codex SDK without an override.
- Real SDK round-trip fixtures with isolated configuration and synthetic endpoints cover independent native readers, warm/cold restores, an initially empty user configuration, and encrypted-history compatibility.
- The ChatGPT desktop UI has not been end-to-end validated; manual verification remains part of this draft.

title: agentHost: Exclude SDK-native skills from directory discovery
body:
## Problem

In Agent Host discovery mode, VS Code combines two Copilot runtime APIs that intentionally return different sets of data:

- `skills.getDiscoveryPaths()` returns directories where users can create skills, such as project, personal, and configured custom directories.
- `skills.discover()` returns every skill available to the runtime, including skills supplied by installed plugins and the runtime itself.

VS Code previously assumed that every item from `skills.discover()` belonged under a directory from `skills.getDiscoveryPaths()`. Copilot runtime 1.0.84-2 exposed that latent mismatch by returning installed-plugin skills. Because plugin and built-in skills do not have user-creatable discovery directories, VS Code created synthetic writable fallback directories for them and emitted an invariant error on every customization refresh:

`[SessionCustomizationDiscovery] BUG: customization '.../installed-plugins/.../SKILL.md' of type 'skill' is outside discovered directories`

In one recent Insiders session this repeated tens of thousands of times. The resulting directory entries were also projected into VS Code's synthetic session plugin even though plugin and built-in skills are SDK-native sources.

## Fix

Exclude skills whose SDK `source` is `plugin` or `builtin` before converting discovered skills into directory customizations.

This keeps the two ownership paths separate:

- SDK-native plugin and built-in skills remain owned and loaded by the Copilot runtime.
- Project, inherited, personal, and custom-directory skills continue to be represented by VS Code directory customizations.

The existing fallback and invariant error remain unchanged for directory-backed customizations that unexpectedly cannot be attributed to a discovery path. Using `excludeHostSkills` on the RPC request would not be appropriate because it would also hide legitimate personal and configured custom-directory skills.

## Testing

Added a regression test that returns plugin, built-in, and project skills from the SDK and verifies that:

- plugin and built-in skills are excluded from directory customizations;
- the project skill remains under its reported discovery directory; and
- no fallback error is emitted for the SDK-native skills.

Validation:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts` - 44 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- pre-commit hygiene checks

(Written by Copilot)

title: agentHost: prevent duplicate Codex skills across sessions
body:
## Summary

Stop registering client-synced plugin skill caches through the process-global `skills/extraRoots/set` API. Those caches are scoped by workspace and revision, so registering their union makes native discovery expose duplicate copies and skills from unrelated sessions.

Replace that delivery path with supported session-scoped behavior:

- Advertise the enabled client skills' names, descriptions, and synced file paths through `turn/start.additionalContext`. Send the current catalogue on every turn, including an explicit empty catalogue after removal.
- Grant read-only access to the session's skill directories through the existing thread permission profiles. Reuse start/resume reconciliation when the directories or permission profile change; preserve existing filesystem restrictions and profile inheritance.
- Keep native skill discovery, including `~/.agents/skills`, separate and unchanged. Do not register generated bundles in the global native catalogue.

The review identified a real gap in the original draft: `thread/resume` cannot update `selectedCapabilityRoots`, and the pinned SDK did not advertise client skills through that path. The revised implementation no longer relies on those roots for client skills. It also avoids `turn/start.permissions` while thread-specific read grants are active, because that field reloads the process-wide profile and drops those grants.

This uses the existing session lifecycle and the pinned SDK; it does not add a new manager, SDK upgrade, or cache migration.

## Validation

- Merged `origin/main` through `978cb41d811` and rebuilt the complete product successfully with the corresponding dependencies.
- **529 Codex unit tests pass.**
- **All 4 Codex provider integration tests pass** with the repository-pinned **Codex 0.149.1**, including the original failing CI assertion that plugin skills reach the actual model request.
- New integration coverage checks add/remove after the first turn, workspace isolation, native user skills, actual shell reads outside workspace/temp roots, read-grant preservation across permission changes, denied unrelated reads and skill writes, preserved workspace writes, and revocation while the cached file remains on disk.
- Launch + dap-cli verification in an isolated Code OSS Agents window with a real ChatGPT-backed Codex model: add one skill to an existing thread, read its body, disable it, and verify that both its current catalogue entry and read grant disappear without replacing the thread. title: Avoid subscribing to untitled Agent Host sessions

## Summary

Fixes #335473.

Avoid opening an Agent Host session-state subscription from the chat input
pills while the workbench resource is still `untitled-*`.

The pills resolved the UI resource synchronously and could issue
`subscribe(claude:/untitled-...)` immediately before first-send materialization
bound a different real backend URI. If that request lost the race, Agent Host
returned `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` and the new session could remain half-bound
indefinitely.

This is a remaining provisional-to-real identity variant of #330531. The
create-before-subscribe ordering from #330761 is present in the reproducing
build, but it cannot make an obsolete untitled URI valid after materialization
changes the identity.

## Fix

- Return no pills resolution while the workbench resource is untitled.
- Let the existing view-model change re-evaluate the pills after the real
  resource is installed.
- Add a regression test asserting that:
  - the untitled resource opens no subscription;
  - changing to the real resource opens the expected real backend subscription.

This matches the existing untitled guards in the Agent Host config chips,
chat-input picker, and customization service.
